title: Practicing subtraction with the Soroban, the Suanpan (算盤) and the Schyoty (счёты)
header: Practicing subtraction with the Soroban, the Suanpan (算盤) and the Schyoty (счёты)

text.text:
### Prerequisites

This text accompanies an application that teaches, step by step, how to perform subtractions using the abacus. For a better understanding of the steps, we suggest first studying the text Subtraction on the abacuses of China (Zhōngguó, 中国), Japan (Nippon-koku or Nihon-koku, 日本国) and Russia before proceeding (<htcite0>).

text.text:
### A next step

Our understanding of subtraction has been evolving throughout the texts and applications published on History Tracers. So far, we have followed these steps:
- We learned that subtraction is the inverse operation of addition.
- We reinforced the idea of borrowing from a higher place value when necessary.
- In the previous game, we advanced the concept of borrowing across multiple digits.

Our next step on this learning path will be to subtract numbers with more than two digits (units, tens, hundreds, etc.) from a single number. Given this scenario, reflect on the following question:

text.text:
Reflection 1: Next step

With everything that has been seen so far, how would you subtract a number with three, four, or even eight digits from another number?

With everything we have seen so far, we can conclude that we should follow exactly the same steps we performed earlier, but repeating them more times.

To better visualize these new steps, we will again use the abacuses developed in China (Zhongguo, 中國), Japan (Nippon-koku or Nihon-koku, 日本国) and Russia.

### The Abacus (Subtraction)

Recognizing the importance of homework exercises as a way to reinforce knowledge (<htcite0>), we present below an abacus that performs a subtraction and explains, step by step, each stage necessary to carry out the calculation using this tool.

#### Levels

The game has 8 levels, one for each column of the abacus. Each level defines the number of digits (the minuend and subtrahend share the same order of magnitude):

- **Level 1**: 1-digit numbers (1 to 9)
- **Level 2**: 2-digit numbers (10 to 19)
- **Level 3**: 3-digit numbers (100 to 199)
- **Level 4**: 4-digit numbers (1,000 to 1,999)
- **Level 5**: 5-digit numbers (10,000 to 19,999)
- **Level 6**: 6-digit numbers (100,000 to 199,999)
- **Level 7**: 7-digit numbers (1,000,000 to 1,999,999)
- **Level 8**: 8-digit numbers (10,000,000 to 19,999,999)

Use the "⭐ Next Level" button to advance through the levels.

#### How to play

Between the bar containing the buttons "🎲 New Exercise" and "⭐ Next Level" and the button "➡️ Next Step", an instruction will be displayed indicating the operations to be performed at the current stage. Upon correctly completing the stage, a message will appear at the bottom of the abacus congratulating you: "✅ Correct! Click 'Next step' to continue."

You should follow the steps until you complete the calculation, at which point you will receive the following message: "🎉🎉🎉 PERFECT! 🎉🎉🎉 Great job using the abacus!".

After you finish the 8th level, you will receive the following message: "🏅 Congratulations! You reached the last level! 🏅"

You may repeat as many exercises as you wish at the same level. To do so, simply click "🎲 New Exercise" after completing a calculation.

source.text: Costa, M., Cardoso, A. P., Lacerda, C., Lopes, A., & Gomes, C.
